2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The cell cores were prepared by stacking with a separator separating the anodes (11) and cathodes (10), and then packaged in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. The resultant pouch cell was dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm. All other preparations involved were carried out using methods commonly used in commercial battery manufacturing.

association_citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ .

citations.quote:
Electrochemical Measurements
Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I). The cell was first charged to 4.0 V and subsequently transferred to an explosion-proof oven (gdw-100 l, Suoyate) for constant $60^{\circ}$ C elevated temperature storage. The cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear cyclic voltammetry scanning tests were performed on an electrochemical workstation (CHI660E, Chenhua, Shanghai). A Solartron 1470 instrument (AMETEK) was used for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests, the frequency range was 100 kHz-0.01 Hz, and simultaneously apply a voltage disturbance of 10 mV.

Electrochemical Measurements
Firstly, the electrolyte was injected into the pouch NNFM111/HC cells in an argon-filled glove box and then the cells were deposited at room temperature for 24 h. The cells were first charged at 0.1 C constant current for 390 min with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . After charging, the cells were put at $45^{\circ}$ C for 24 h with a pressure of $3 \, kg cm^{-2}$ . All cells were activated by charging and discharging at 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, and 1 C. The charge and discharge tests of the NNFM111/HC full cells were conducted using a battery test system (CT-3008 W, Neware, China) at a voltage range of 2.0-4.0 V. The cycle performance of NNFM111/HC full cells was measured at a constant temperature of $25^{\circ}$ C and $45^{\circ}$ C with a charge and discharge current of 1 C. The discharge curves of the NNFM111/HC full cells at $-20^{\circ}$ C were measured in a temperature controlled test chamber at the discharge rates of 0.5 C and 1 C. The ratio of the discharge capacity of the cell at $-20^{\circ}$ C to the last discharge capacity of the cell activated at room temperature was taken as the capacity retention rate of the cell at low temperature. The cells with 50% state of charge (SOC) discharged at a current rate of 2 C for 10 s at $-20^{\circ}$ C. The direct current resistance (DCR) was calculated on the basis of Ohm's law (R=U/I). The cell was first charged to 4.0 V and subsequently transferred to an explosion-proof oven (gdw-100 l, Suoyate) for constant $60^{\circ}$ C elevated temperature storage. The cyclic voltammetry (CV) and linear cyclic voltammetry scanning tests were performed on an electrochemical workstation (CHI660E, Chenhua, Shanghai). A Solartron 1470 instrument (AMETEK) was used for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests, the frequency range was 100 kHz-0.01 Hz, and simultaneously apply a voltage disturbance of 10 mV.

3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2
citations.quote:
A B S T R A C T
A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

association_citations.quote:
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.quote: The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first. Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ .

review.experimental_association: The cited performance and corrosion observations come from the same Fan et al. study that prepared the exact NaPF6-E formulation (0.8 M NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7) in NFM||HC pouch cells with Al-substrate electrodes in a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch, so the formulation, cell chemistry, and test platform correspond to the target. The -10 °C cycling result (Fig. 4g/h) is measured on these NaPF6-E pouch cells and is the direct low-temperature evidence.

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：candidate-1（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC, EMC, DEC；溶剂比例（质量）：DEC=1, EC=1, EMC=6, PC=2。
- 配方原文 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . All electrolytes were prepared in an argon-filled glove box with $H_{2}O$ and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm.

### 候选资料：candidate-2（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；总盐浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaFSI：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, PC, EMC, DEC；溶剂比例（质量）：DEC=1, EC=1, EMC=6, PC=2。
- 配方原文 [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), $NaPF_{6}$ and NaFSI used in the electrolyte are all from the commercial products of Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. and not further purified. The blank electrolyte was a mixture of 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 (by weight). NaFSI was added to the blank electrolyte to replace part of $NaPF_{6}$ , maintaining the total content of NaFSI and $NaPF_{6}$ at 1 M. In this work, "blank" represents 1 M $NaPF_{6}$ , "0.1 M NaFSI" represents 0.1 M $NaFSI + 0.9 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.3 M NaFSI" represents 0.3 M $NaFSI + 0.7 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.5 M NaFSI" represents 0.5 M $NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.7 M NaFSI" represents 0.7 M $NaFSI + 0.3 M NaPF_{6}$ , "0.9 M NaFSI" represents 0.9 M $NaFSI + 0.1 M NaPF_{6}$ . ### 候选资料：candidate-3（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=3, EMC=7；添加剂：trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS)；添加剂用量：TMSS=3 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

### 候选资料：candidate-4（尚未获推荐）

盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=3, EMC=7；添加剂：trimethylsilyl benzenesulfonate (TMSBS)；添加剂用量：TMSBS=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

### 候选资料：candidate-5（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaFSI；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaFSI：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3, EMC=7。
- 配方原文 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). Three electrolytes with 0.8 M concentration were all prepared by dissolving sodium salt in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and the electrolytes were represented as X-E, where X was the lithium salt used. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) active material was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, hard carbon (HC) active material was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using a NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a HC (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a celgard 2700 separator. For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate.

### 候选资料：candidate-6（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3, EMC=7。
- 配方原文 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec5::child0]：Ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaFSI, $NaPF_{6}$ and NaDFOB ( $\geq98\%$ ) were also provided by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd (Table S1). For the preparation of NFM cathode, NFM, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. For the HC anode, HC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate.

### 候选资料：candidate-7（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3, EMC=7；添加剂：sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP)；添加剂用量：NaDFP=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec4::child0]：EC, EMC, and sodium flurophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7, and this electrolyte was assigned as baseline electrolyte. NaDFP was added to the baseline electrolyte to prepare. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd and Hard Carbon were purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. Pouch cells were assembled using an NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1C), a hard carbon (HC, 290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05C) anode, and a Celgard 2700 membrane as the separator. NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate. The areal loading of the anode and cathode was 16 g m $^{-2}$ and 33 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively.

## 候选评估
### candidate-1
评估建议：Candidate-1 is precisely the paper's single-salt NaPF6 'blank' electrolyte, which satisfies the collector/shell non-corrosion requirement but is the weaker low-temperature baseline: the same work shows the blank system's -20 C capacity/recovery is clearly below the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt, and no -10 C data exist for it, so low-temperature suitability for the -10 C target is not established and the candidate is held rather than recommended.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte salt is 1.0 M NaPF6 (single salt, no additive)：The source's 'blank' electrolyte is exactly 1 M NaPF6, and the candidate's salt/concentration match it. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Solvent system is EC/PC/EMC/DEC in 1:2:6:1 mass ratio：The blank electrolyte is described as EC, PC, EMC and DEC at 1:2:6:1 by weight, matching candidate-1's solvent set and mass basis. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Cell chemistry is NFM (NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2) cathode with hard-carbon anode：The paper studies NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2/hard-carbon (NNFM111/HC) sodium-ion cells, matching the NFM||HC target. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec1::child0]
- Pouch-cell format：The electrochemical measurements were made on pouch NNFM111/HC cells, matching the target pouch format. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5]
- No observed Al current-collector or stainless-steel shell corrosion：For the single NaPF6 system both the aluminum foil and the stainless-steel sheets show higher stability with rapid current convergence, and the single-NaPF6 electrolyte remained clear and original after cycling, i.e. no corrosion products. Note this was observed in two-electrode Al/Na and stainless-steel/Na electrolytic cells rather than the pouch full cell. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child5][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child7]
- Low-temperature operation at the target -10 C：The source reports low-temperature data only at -20 C for the NNFM111/HC full cell, not at -10 C, and no explicit transfer to -10 C is stated; moreover at -20 C the single-salt (blank) system retained far less capacity than the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt (about 0 vs ~200 mAh at high rate), suggesting the baseline is weak but no -10 C measurement supports the target. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate's chemistry, salt, solvent ratios and pouch full-cell testing are directly matched by the paper's 'blank' 1 M NaPF6 electrolyte in NNFM111/HC pouch cells, which supports the identity of the candidate. The corrosion evidence for the Al foil and stainless-steel shell, however, comes from separate two-electrode Al/Na and stainless-steel/Na electrolytic cells, not from the pouch full cell, so it is a limited material-compatibility association rather than a full-cell corrosion demonstration. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child5][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5]
### candidate-2
评估建议：The candidate reproduces the paper's best-performing formulation (0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6 in 1:2:6:1 EC/PC/EMC/DEC) and shows favorable -20 C behavior, but the program's hard condition of 'no observed collector or shell corrosion' is not met: for this exact electrolyte the paper observes residual holes on the Al foil, and stainless-steel absence of corrosion and exact -10 C performance are not directly demonstrated. Hence a held, not recommended, decision.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Dual-salt NaFSI/NaPF6 at 0.5 M + 0.5 M (total 1 M) as the salt system：The paper defines the blank electrolyte as 1 M NaPF6 replaced in part by NaFSI at fixed total 1 M, with the explicit label 0.5 M NaFSI = 0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6, matching the candidate's salt combination and concentrations. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- Solvent system EC/PC/EMC/DEC at 1:2:6:1 by weight：The base electrolyte is stated as 1 M NaPF6 in EC, PC, EMC and DEC with a ratio of 1:2:6:1 by weight, identical to the candidate's EC:PC:EMC:DEC = 1:2:6:1 mass ratio. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0]
- No observed corrosion of the Al current collector：For the 0.5 M NaFSI double-salt electrolyte the paper reports on its Al foil that surface cracks disappear but 'only a few holes' remain, i.e. residual pitting/traces are actually observed, so the strict 'no observed corrosion' claim is not satisfied by the same candidate under its direct SEM observation. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child8]
- No observed corrosion of the stainless-steel cell shell：The paper shows double-salt addition reduces corrosion currents of stainless-steel/Na cells and that single NaPF6 is stable, but it only reports reduced (comparative) corrosion for the double-salt system and gives no direct negative observation (e.g. SEM of intact SS surface) for the 0.5 M NaFSI electrolyte. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child5][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec7::child10]
- Low-temperature operation at -10 C：The paper directly measures low-temperature performance only at -20 C (improved 0.5C/1C capacity and reduced DCR), not at the target -10 C, and states no explicit transfer relation to -10 C, so the exact target temperature is not directly evidenced. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child9]
- Target cell format: NFM||hard-carbon pouch cell：The study is built on NNFM111/HC (Na-Ni-Fe-Mn layered oxide vs hard carbon) pouch full cells, the same electrode couple and pouch format as the target. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec1::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec5]
文献与候选的关联：The candidate matches the paper's electrolyte preparation exactly (0.5 M NaFSI + 0.5 M NaPF6, total 1 M, in EC:PC:EMC:DEC 1:2:6:1 by weight) and is tested in NNFM111/HC pouch full cells, with Al-foil and stainless-steel corrosion probed by LSV/CV and SEM. The association is thus established for salt, solvent, ratio and cell chemistry; the only mismatch is temperature (-20 C reported vs -10 C target), so low-temperature support is at a harsher but different condition. [0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec3::child0][0015_Fan 等 - 2024 - A Sodium Bisfluorosulfonylimide NaFSI-based Multifunctional Electrolyte Stabilizes the Performan::sec8::child2]
### candidate-3
评估建议：The candidate matches the paper's electrolyte identity and is directly demonstrated in pouch NFM/HC cells at -10 C, so the low-temperature and cell-format requirements are met. However, the program's hard requirement of no observed collector or shell corrosion is not documented in any source, and the stainless-steel shell is never specified, so a recommendation cannot be issued; hold pending corrosion-specific evidence.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Salt identity and concentration: NaPF6 at 1.0 mol/L：The paper prepares baseline electrolyte by dissolving NaPF6 at 1 mol/L, matching the candidate salt and concentration. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0]
- Solvent system EC:EMC in 3:7 mass ratio：The formula uses cyclic EC and linear EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7, identical to the candidate's solvent ratio basis. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0]
- Functional additive TMSS at 3 wt%：The paper augments the baseline with 3 wt% TMSS as the functional additive, matching the candidate's additive and loading. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7]
- Target cell format: pouch NFM/hard-carbon cell：The work evaluates the TMSS electrolyte in pouch NFM/hard-carbon cells, which is the requested cell chemistry and format. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13]
- Low-temperature operation at -10 C：Fig. 3c reports pouch NFM/HC cycling at -10 C with 0.3C charge/0.5C discharge, where the TMSS electrolyte retained higher capacity than baseline, directly supporting -10 C performance of this candidate. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13]
- Al current collector present in the tested configuration：The NFM cathode slurry is coated onto an aluminium substrate in the pouch cell build, so the candidate electrolyte is used against an Al current collector; this establishes Al is present but not that corrosion is absent. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0]
- Stainless-steel shell in the tested configuration：No source describes the pouch cell shell material (e.g., stainless steel), so compatibility with a stainless-steel shell is not evidenced. 
- No observed collector or shell corrosion (negative fact)：The paper reports no obvious gas evolution and good cycling, but never inspects or reports absence of Al-collector or shell corrosion; general performance cannot substitute for a direct negative corrosion observation. 
文献与候选的关联：The candidate formula is identified in sec7 (1 mol/L NaPF6, EC:EMC 3:7 by mass, 3 wt% TMSS) and the same components/assembly are described in sec4/sec4::child0 (slurry coated on Al substrate, pouch NFM/HC build). sec7::child13 then reports the -10 C pouch NFM/HC cycling of this TMSS-containing electrolyte versus baseline, linking the formula identity to the target low-temperature cell test.
